subject: Order Form: SLA redlines — response windows, maintenance carveouts
messages:

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form SLA — proposed edits

Hannah,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. Procurement reviewed the SLA and have a few concrete asks before legal will sign:

- Uptime target: Can you confirm a 99.95% monthly uptime floor (our procurement requires this for platform-critical integrations).
- Service credits: We need credits to scale up to 25% for sustained outages >4 hours cumulative in a 30-day period.
- Response times: For P1 incidents we require a 1-hour initial response and a 4-hour remediation ETA for the first triage update.
- Maintenance: We need a blackout window exclusion for our quarterly big-batch ETL runs (one weekend per quarter, listed dates).

I've attached our redline (ACME_OrderForm_SLA_redlines.pdf) with inline comments. Can legal confirm what is negotiable vs. deal-breaking? We are targeting an internal approval by next Wednesday.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

Elena Rossi

Jonas / Lauren — forwarding ACME's redline and procurement asks. Key asks summarized below (see attached redline_sla_track_changes.docx for proposed language):

- 99.95% monthly uptime floor (procurement says must be explicit).
- Service credits escalated to 25% for >4h cumulative outage in 30d.
- P1 initial response = 1 hour; first remediation update = 4 hours.
- Quarterly blackout exclusion for scheduled ETL windows (ACME will provide dates).

Questions / concerns from our side:
1) 99.95% is materially higher than our standard 99.9% for shared hosted customers — affects credit exposure and capacity carveouts.
2) 25% credit cap for sustained outages is heavy; we typically cap at 15% for order forms with a dedicated-support add-on.
3) The 1-hour P1 response is reasonable operationally if we pin on supported channels and a dedicated on-call for the account; need to confirm whether this requires a support SOW / premium tier.

Proposed next steps:
- Jonas: can you review the uptime/credit math and propose a capped compromise (e.g., 99.94% floor + 20% credit cap with annual credit cap aggregate)?
- Lauren: legal to review redline and flag language we cannot accept as-is (esp. indemnities and ambiguous maintenance carveouts).
- I'll book a 30-min alignment call with ACME + our ops/legal tomorrow if possible.

CC'd Elena so she sees who will take the lead on each item.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 10:02 AM hannah.schmitt@redwood.com wrote:
> Jonas / Lauren — forwarding ACME's redline and procurement asks. Key asks summarized below (see attached redline_sla_track_changes.docx for proposed language):

Thanks, Hannah. Quick operational read:

- Uptime: moving from 99.9% to 99.95% increases monthly allowable downtime from ~43 minutes to ~21 minutes. That's material but not impossible. If we accept the floor we should:
  * narrow the definition of "Downtime" (exclude customer-reported interruptions that are third-party-caused), and
  * add a single rolling 12-month aggregate cap on credits to limit runaway exposure.
- Credits: I can support 20% as a compromise if we also include an annual cap at, say, 50% of the annual contract value for credits and require that credits are the sole remedy (no additional refunds).
- P1 response: 1-hour initial ack is OK if we require incidents to be reported via the designated support channel and tracked in the ticketing system; remediation ETAs are fine as SLAs only for supported platforms (dedicated VPC / dedicated capacity).
- Maintenance blackout: operationally we can carve out one weekend per quarter if ACME gives the dates 60 days in advance and those windows cannot be used to claim credits.

I'll draft suggested clause language and mark areas that must remain high-level in the MSA (to avoid per-account indemnity expansion).

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment (draft): sla_uptime_credit_compromise.txt (text, 3 KB)

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Elena — thanks for the clear redlines and timeline. Based on Jonas and Lauren's initial read:

- Redwood can agree to a revised uptime floor of 99.94% (compromise) with tightened Downtime definitions and an annual credit cap.
- We'll propose a step-down credit schedule that reaches 20% (not 25%) for outages >4h, with a per-year credit ceiling (draft language attached).
- P1 initial response = 1 hour (acknowledgement). We will include a requirement that incidents are opened via the agreed support channel and that the account purchases the Dedicated Support Add-on for the 4-hour remediation ETA guarantee.
- Maintenance blackout: we can accept one weekend per quarter as a non-creditable scheduled blackout provided ACME supplies dates 60 days in advance.

Next steps:
1) Lauren — please confirm legal sign-off on the proposed bullet points and the attached tracked doc. If you can provide redline-friendly language today we'll send back an order-form counter to ACME this afternoon.
2) Elena — if the above is acceptable, please confirm and we'll route the counter for DocuSign; we will add the credit cap and dedicated-support SOW as referenced.
